hands_on_tech.overview: October 2026 commercial generative AI video production toolchain. Seamlessly bridges cutting-edge multi-model AI video generation (Adobe Firefly Video, Google Flow / Veo 2 & 3, Kling AI v1.5/v2, Runway Gen-3 Alpha / Turbo) with enterprise non-linear timeline editing in Adobe Premiere Pro 2026, hybrid compositing and planar tracking in Adobe After Effects 2026, high-fidelity reference frame engineering in Adobe Photoshop, studio voice synthesis in ElevenLabs, Hollywood node-based color grading in DaVinci Resolve 21, and broadcast 4K upscaling in Topaz Video AI.

software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.credit_budget_and_anti_burn_protocol: Cloud generative compute is metered across platforms. To protect student resources, the program enforces a mandatory 3-Tier Draft-to-Hero protocol: Tier 1 ideation and prompt testing in Claude/ChatGPT and Midjourney Relaxed mode; Tier 2 motion blocking in fast/turbo modes (Runway Gen-3 Turbo / Kling Standard); Tier 3 single-pass hero renders in full-credit engines. Zero promises of unlimited credits are made.
software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.ethical_likeness_and_voice_rights_govern: Strict prohibition against synthesizing real-person celebrity likenesses, public figures, or cloning human voices without verifiable, written commercial consent. All character workflows leverage synthetic personas, customized turnaround sheets, or authorized digital ambassadors.
software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.commercial_safety_and_indemnification: Delineates enterprise-grade, legally indemnified models (Adobe Firefly Video, trained on licensed Adobe Stock) from research-oriented open or semi-closed models. Students learn C2PA Content Credentials, watermark mitigation, and commercial release documentation.
software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.zero_cost_local_production_stack: DaVinci Resolve 21 Free edition is utilized for Hollywood-grade color grading and Fairlight audio post, providing full node trees, scopes, and -14 LUFS loudness mastering at zero software cost. Creative Cloud tools run on standard student licenses without unreleased experimental beta dependencies.

faq.question: Who can join the Generative AI Video Production Professional program?
faq.answer: This course is open to beginners with basic computer literacy, content creators, video editors, graphic designers, marketing creatives, and aspiring video producers seeking professional mastery of generative video pipelines. No prior filmmaking degree or coding knowledge is required.

faq.question: Is previous video editing required before enrolling?
faq.answer: No. Previous video editing experience is not required. The program is structured progressively. Month 1 builds foundational visual storytelling grammar, shot sizes, framing, and scriptwriting before introducing hands-on editing in Premiere Pro (Month 3) and After Effects (Month 4). However, students with basic computer navigation skills will advance most rapidly.

faq.question: What does 'AI-first commercial video training' mean?
faq.answer: It means generative AI tools are not taught as isolated gimmicks, but as core production engines integrated directly into an industry-standard post-production workflow. You learn to direct AI models to generate shots based on real commercial scripts, and then edit, composite, grade, and finish those shots in Premiere Pro, After Effects, and DaVinci Resolve.

faq.question: Why is the program structured across 5 months and 200 guided hours?
faq.answer: Mastering commercial AI video requires both generative proficiency and professional post-production craft. Across 200 guided hours (40 hours per month), students master pre-production (Mo. 1), video generation and consistency (Mo. 2), Premiere Pro editing (Mo. 3), After Effects compositing and audio (Mo. 4), and commercial campaigns with capstone portfolio production (Mo. 5).

faq.question: Which generative AI video models are taught in the course?
faq.answer: The program provides deep hands-on training across Adobe Firefly Video, Google Flow (utilizing supported Veo video models), Kling AI (v1.5/v2), and Runway (Gen-2 / Gen-3 Alpha). Students learn model selection based on cost, control, camera physics, and rendering quality.

faq.question: How is Adobe Firefly integrated into the commercial workflow?
faq.answer: Adobe Firefly is used for commercially safe text-to-image and text-to-video generation, reference-guided frame expansion, Firefly Boards pre-visualization, and direct integration with Adobe Photoshop and Premiere Pro Generative Extend.

faq.question: How are Google Flow and supported Veo models utilized?
faq.answer: Google Flow and supported Veo video models are used for high-fidelity cinematic camera motions, text-to-video scene generation, start/end-frame interpolation, and multi-shot visual planning with cinematic depth.

faq.question: What role does Kling AI play in the production pipeline?
faq.answer: Kling AI is deployed for complex subject motion, photorealistic human movement, start-frame to end-frame camera transitions, and controlled image-to-video generation requiring high temporal consistency.

faq.question: How is Runway (Gen-2 / Gen-3 Alpha) deployed?
faq.answer: Runway Gen-3 Alpha is utilized for high-speed dynamic camera movements, camera control brushes, text-to-video, image-to-video, and generating atmospheric environment plates for VFX compositing.

faq.question: Why is Adobe Photoshop included in a video production course?
faq.answer: Photoshop is essential for visual asset development in Month 1 and Module 04: generating clean reference plates, removing AI generation artifacts, fixing anatomical anomalies, masking clean product plates, and creating graphic title overlays for video editing.

faq.question: Why is Adobe Premiere Pro the primary editorial backbone?
faq.answer: Generative video clips are meaningless without precise editorial storytelling. Premiere Pro (Module 07 & 08) provides classical 3-point timeline assembly, trim mechanics, J/L cut pacing, Text-Based Editing, Auto Reframe, and Enhance Speech audio cleanup.

faq.question: How is Adobe After Effects used for hybrid compositing and motion design?
faq.answer: In Module 09, After Effects is used to composite synthetic AI environment plates with filmed live-action talent, perform Mocha AE planar screen tracking on mobile devices, extract moving subjects with Roto Brush 3, and animate commercial kinetic typography.

faq.question: How does ElevenLabs power the commercial audio workflow?
faq.answer: ElevenLabs is taught in Module 10 for professional commercial voiceover engineering: script pacing, stability/clarity tuning, emotional inflection, SSML phonetic controls, multilingual voice cloning, and authorized voice-consent documentation.

faq.question: Why is DaVinci Resolve 21 taught for color grading?
faq.answer: Disparate AI video engines output mismatched color temperatures, contrast curves, and black levels. DaVinci Resolve 21 Color page is used to balance exposures via video scopes (Waveform, Vectorscope), lock skin tones, and apply unified cinematic film LUTs.

faq.question: When and how is Topaz Video AI deployed?
faq.answer: Topaz Video AI is deployed in Module 10 for neural video enhancement: upscaling 720p/1080p AI clips to crisp 4K, removing synthetic noise and compression artifacts with the Proteus model, restoring facial detail via the Iris model, and interpolating 24fps video to smooth 60fps with Chronos.

faq.question: How does the curriculum solve character and product consistency across shots?
faq.answer: Module 06 teaches systematic character and product consistency: locked turnaround reference sheets, seed parameters, style reference matching (`--sref` / image prompts), clean-plate masking in Photoshop, and start/end-frame anchor workflows.

faq.question: How do start-frame and end-frame animation workflows work?
faq.answer: In supported engines like Kling AI and Runway, students generate a specific start keyframe and end keyframe, directing the AI model to compute the in-between camera motion and subject transformations accurately without hallucinating unpredictable endings.

faq.question: How are real filmed footage and AI-generated elements composited together?
faq.answer: Module 09 and Project 04 teach hybrid plate compositing: extracting filmed actors using green screen or Roto Brush 3, matching camera perspective and horizon lines to AI environment plates, adding artificial contact shadows, equalizing camera sensor grain, and applying edge light wraps.

faq.question: What are the five mandatory portfolio projects?
faq.answer: Students complete 5 assessed projects: P1: AI Commercial Pre-production Kit (treatment deck & script); P2: Cinematic AI Product Teaser (15s luxury product reveal); P3: Performance-Ready Social Media Video (9:16 vertical ad with A/B hooks); P4: Hybrid AI + Live-Action Commercial Shot (VFX composite); and P5: Final AI Commercial Advertising Campaign (12-asset capstone suite) plus a 60–90-second showreel.

faq.question: What is the Final Commercial Advertising Campaign capstone project?
faq.answer: The capstone (Module 13) is a comprehensive commercial campaign for an enterprise brief containing a 30s master commercial, 15s cutdown, 6s bumper, 2 alternative opening hooks, 9:16 and 16:9 exports, storyboard, editable project files, prompt logs, consent evidence, and a signed technical QC report.

faq.question: What are the minimum hardware and computer requirements?
faq.answer: A modern 64-bit Windows 10/11 or macOS computer with a multi-core processor (Intel i5/i7/i9, AMD Ryzen, or Apple Silicon M-series), 16GB RAM minimum (32GB recommended), dedicated GPU with 4GB+ VRAM (NVIDIA RTX recommended for AI features), 250GB+ SSD storage, and 50+ Mbps high-speed internet.

faq.question: What are the legal rules for voice and likeness permissions in synthetic media?
faq.answer: Module 12 enforces strict legal governance: cloning living individuals without signed talent release contracts is prohibited. Students learn to draft voice and likeness consent releases, comply with publicity rights, and maintain ethical synthetic media authorizations.

faq.question: What are the commercial rights and copyright boundaries for AI-generated video?
faq.answer: Module 12 covers commercial licensing tiers across all tools, public domain vs copyrighted training data, human authorship thresholds required for copyright registration, and avoidance of proprietary brand trademarks.

faq.question: What is the difference between this course, Professional Video Editing (4 Months), and the 8-Month Flagship?
faq.answer: The core difference lies in technical orientation: Professional Video Editing (4 Months / 160h) focuses primarily on classical non-linear editing, multicam, Photoshop graphics, and DaVinci color grading for filmed footage. Generative AI Video Production Professional (5 Months / 200h) is an AI-first commercial specialization focusing on generative models (Firefly, Veo, Kling, Runway), synthetic consistency, and hybrid VFX. The 8-Month Flagship is a comprehensive diploma covering both classical editing, full 3D motion design, and advanced broadcast pipelines.
